input: Repot the overgrown peace lily on the windowsill

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is just a straight repot or also involves dividing the plant, trimming roots, or refreshing fertiliser changes the steps and materials needed.
The current pot size and root situation determine what size new pot to buy and whether any roots need cutting, affecting preparation steps.
Whether the user has potting mix, a new pot, and tools already on hand determines whether a supply run is needed before starting.
Knowing where they plan to do the repotting (indoors, outdoors, balcony) affects prep for mess and cleanup steps.
If someone else in the household is responsible or helping, task ownership and coordination steps change.
The user may have a preference for potting mix type (peat-free, specific brand) or pot material (plastic, terracotta, self-watering) which affects what to buy.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — just surviving the repot vs. thriving and blooming — shapes how thorough the aftercare steps should be.

gold.taskDescription: Repot the peace lily on the windowsill into a larger container so it has room to grow and stays healthy.

questions.title: Are you repotting only, or also dividing the plant?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the task is a simple size-up repot or also involves splitting the peace lily into multiple plants.

questions.title: What size is the current pot right now?
questions.description: Knowing the current pot diameter helps determine the correct next pot size to buy or use.

questions.title: Do you already have a new pot and fresh potting mix?
questions.description: Establishes whether a supply run is a prerequisite step before repotting can begin.

questions.title: Where will you do the repotting — indoors or outside?
questions.description: Determines whether prep steps like laying down newspaper or moving to a balcony are needed to manage soil mess.

questions.title: Is this something you are doing alone?
questions.description: Clarifies if another person is involved or responsible, which affects how the task steps are assigned.

questions.title: Do you have a preference for pot material or soil type?
questions.description: Some people prefer terracotta over plastic, or peat-free compost, which affects the shopping and prep steps.

questions.title: What does success look like — just surviving, or blooming again?
questions.description: Shapes how detailed the aftercare plan should be, including watering schedule, humidity tips, and fertilising steps.
